result.title: A Hierarchical Tokenization Framework for Voxel-Level fMRI Representation Learning
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. Code available at https://github.com/su-karanps/HBAR
result.summary: We introduce HBAR (Hierarchical Brain Activity Representation), a hierarchical tokenization framework for learning compact, multi-scale representations of neuroimaging data. HBAR organizes voxel-level resting-state fMRI into a hierarchy spanning sub-parcel voxel groups, parcels, and large-scale functional networks, enabling up to 415x compression while preserving fine-grained spatial information beyond conventional parcellation. The framework supports fixed atlas-based, fully learned, and softly prior-guided hierarchies, allowing us to systematically study the role of structured priors in brain representation learning. On HCP-YA, at approximately 415x compression, HBAR achieves higher parcel and network correlations than rate-matched flat tokenizers, while at a lower 52x compression rate, shuffling the anatomical grouping reduces parcel correlation from 0.920 to 0.886. Demographic readouts with autoregressive training also reveal potential gains from the hierarchical structure. By combining sub-parcel inputs, compact discrete tokens, and multiscale brain structure, HBAR offers a practical framework for representation learning in high-dimensional neuroimaging data.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 HBAR，将体素级静息态 fMRI 组织为「子分区体素组—分区—大尺度功能网络」的层级化 tokenizer，支持固定图谱、完全学习与软先验引导三种层级，在 HCP-YA 上以最高约 415 倍压缩获得高于同压缩率平坦 tokenizer 的分区与网络相关性，并考察人口学读出。
AI.relevance_reason: 其多尺度层级化离散 token 与「高压缩下仍保留细粒度空间信息」的评估方式（压缩率匹配比较、打乱解剖分组的消融）可能为 LVR 中视觉 token 的层级组织与信息坍缩诊断提供参考，但模态与任务差异较大，可供核查迁移可行性。
